title: Uniform equicontinuity in the row variable from joint continuity on a compact domain
statement:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses, and suppose in addition that $Y$ is compact and that $(x,y) \mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous on $X \times Y$. Then $f$ is uniformly equicontinuous in its first argument, uniformly over all columns: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\rho > 0$ such that for all $x, x' \in X$ and all $y \in Y$,
\[
  \dist(x, x') < \rho \;\Longrightarrow\; |f(x,y) - f(x',y)| < \varepsilon.
\]
hypotheses_covered: convex-compact minimax hypotheses hold for X, Y, f
f is jointly continuous on X × Y
replaced:
